images.title: Each rule gets closer
images.purpose: Show on one number line how the calendar total for 1000 years moves closer to the Earth's 365242.2 days as each leap year rule is added.
images.composition: One long horizontal number line across the middle of the frame with three rule markers and one Earth marker, labels alternating above and below so nothing overlaps.
exact_structure: 1 horizontal grey #6B7280 number line from 365240 at the left end to 365250 at the right end, with 11 evenly spaced unnumbered ticks (one for each whole number from 365240 to 365250); the marker labels give the values
Marker at 365250 (right end): vermilion #D55E00 dot, label above 'Every 4th year: 365250'
Marker at 365240 (left end): amber #E69F00 dot, label below 'Not the 100th: 365240'
Marker at 365242: green #009E73 dot, label below 'But the 400th: 365242'
Marker at 365242.2: reddish purple #CC79A7 star, a fifth of a tick space to the right of the green dot, label above 'Earth: 365242.2'
1 caption line under the line: 'Days in 1000 years'
rejection: any marker placed at the wrong value, or the Earth star placed left of the green dot
any day total other than 365240, 365242, 365242.2 and 365250
the ticks numbered separately, repeating the marker values
images.takeaway: Every 4th year overshoots by 7.8 days, leaving out the 100th falls 2.2 days short, and bringing back the 400th leaves a gap of only 0.2 day in 1000 years.
images.description: A number line from 365240 to 365250 with dots for each leap rule's total over 1000 years and a star for the Earth at 365242.2, nearest the 400th year rule's 365242.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on the 100th and 400th year rules.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which dot is nearest the star, and by how much each dot misses it.

image_decisions.why: A number line shows at a glance how each rule narrows the gap to the Earth.
